correctness.rationale: I rebuilt the rim/rung graph and independently enumerated matchings by treating the lowest available graph vertex as either unmatched or joined to one available neighbor. The repaired toggling rule gives 117732 faces including the empty face, 714010 nonempty-poset cover incidences, 58845 matched pairs, and only one critical vertex and forty six-cells at n=10. In a directed cycle the disjoint matching forces alternation of up and down steps. The earliest used toggle must be undone by a downward step whose two faces were both available at that stage; that cover would instead have been matched. Thus the repaired proof supplies a direct acyclicity argument. Discrete Morse theory gives a one-point skeleton below dimension six, so the six-cells each attach trivially and the space is a wedge of forty S^6. This is 5-connected but not 6-connected; the covered smaller cases have nonzero reduced integral homology in some degree at most five. As a check on the frozen table I also reduced integral incidence relations in topological order, obtaining the zero 2x2 matrix at n=5, the identical nonzero rows (1,0,−1,0,0,0,0,0) at n=8 and an identity minor in rows 3 and 14 at n=9. Unit pivots cancel corresponding sphere–cell pairs: attaching maps to the lower d-sphere wedge are determined by degrees via Hurewicz (d≥2), and unimodular basis changes are realized by wedge homotopy equivalences of source and target. This substantiates the integral homotopy claims, not just the reported mod-two homology. No recurrence is inferred.
